transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, the main reason I’m here is that I'm having a really hard time at work with anything that takes real, sitting-down brain work. I manage health services, and whenever I have to do my monthly reports or sit down to plan a multi-site health event... I don't know, it just feels like I hit a wall. I keep putting those tasks off, even when I know how much they matter and that I need to get them done. It's just getting to be a real problem.
Did you have similar problems with focus or completing schoolwork when you were a child?

Yeah, I did. Even back in elementary school, my teachers would tell my parents that I was bright, but... I was always daydreaming. I would lose my worksheets all the time, and I was always forgetting to actually turn in my homework. Honestly, the only way things got handed in was because my mother checked my backpack every single night to make sure I did it.
Do you often feel restless or like you have to fidget or keep moving?

Not really, no. I mean, I can sit still just fine. It's not like my body needs to be moving around or anything. It's more just... getting my brain to actually focus on the work in front of me that's the hard part. But physically, no, I don't really have an issue with feeling restless or needing to fidget.
Do you avoid social situations because you worry about being criticized or rejected?

No, not at all. I don't really have any issues with social situations. I mean, my job involves coordinating with a lot of different people, and I'm perfectly comfortable with that. I don't worry about being rejected or criticized or anything like that. It's really just the administrative, solitary work that gives me trouble, not the people part.
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling down or depressed most days?

No, I haven't. I mean, I get a little frustrated with myself sometimes when I fall behind on my paperwork at the clinic, but... no, I wouldn't say I feel depressed or down. My mood is generally perfectly fine.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things most days?

No, I wouldn't say that. I'm not really much of a worrier. I mean, obviously I think about work and making sure the clinic runs smoothly, but it's not like a constant worry or anything. I don't really stress about things outside of just the normal day-to-day stuff.
Do you also have these attention and organization problems in other parts of your life, like at home or with personal tasks?

Yeah, it does affect things outside of work. I mean, I'm still getting by at the clinic and out in the community, but... well, it's taking a toll. People have had to step in and cover gaps for me when I miss things, and deadlines have definitely slipped. It's frustrating because I've embarrassed myself having to make all these last-minute apologies—not just to my coworkers, but to my friends, too, when I drop the ball on personal stuff.
